newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha weakens as buyers remain elusive.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha weakens as buyers remain elusive.

text.p: NWE naphtha weakened on Friday as a lack of buying interest in the region pressured prices lower, traders said.
Traders said a Dutch end-user was offering a 13,000-14,000 tonne Russian cargo at $182 cif Rotterdam, down from $185 on Thursday, but so far the player had only received bids around $176 and $178.
A European-based trading house bought a 12,000-13,000 tonne pipeline spec cargo out of Grangemouth for $186.50 to cover part of a commitment to a major European petrochemical company.
Swaps, meanwhile, were steady talked at $185/$186 fob ARA for April.
Traders said the Asian arbitrage door remained tightly shut, but added that lower prices could trigger more buying in Europe next week.

Already toward the end of this week, a German petrochemical firm was reported to have picked up a couple of cargoes -- one off a French refiner and a second off a Spanish player -- in direct deals. -- Melanie Goodfellow, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7714.
